topic: 128-bit Integer Multiplication and Division in x86-64
explanation: x86-64 architecture supports 128-bit arithmetic operations, enabling calculations beyond the standard 64-bit register size.  This is crucial for handling very large integers, exceeding the capacity of a single 64-bit register.  The operations use a pair of registers (%rdx and %rax) to represent the 128-bit result, improving precision for applications requiring high-range arithmetic.

extraction_metadata.source: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)

book: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
code_example:
; Unsigned Multiply (64b * 64b -> 128b)
mov %rdi, %rax      ; Operand 1 (Low)
mov %rsi, %rbx      ; Operand 2
mul %rbx            ; RDX:RAX = RDI * RSI

; Signed Multiply (64b * 64b -> 128b)
mov %rdi, %rax
mov %rsi, %rbx
imul %rbx           ; RDX:RAX = RDI * RSI

; Signed Division (128b / 64b)
mov %rdi, %rax      ; Load 64b Dividend
cqo                 ; Sign extend RAX to RDX:RAX (128b dividend)
mov %rsi, %rbx      ; Divisor
idiv %rbx           ; Q=RAX, R=RDX

; Unsigned Division (128b / 64b)
mov %rdx, %rdx      ; Dividend High (Must be explicit)
mov %rax, %rax      ; Dividend Low
mov %rbx, %rbx      ; Divisor
div %rbx            ; Q=RAX, R=RDX
keywords: x86 128-bit multiplication, rdx rax register pair, x86-64 wide division
